intro: Potsdam's thickest protected oak is called the thousand-year oak, and nobody has ever measured the thousand years. It stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, 685 centimetres round, with four more protected oaks a short walk away. Ten of the fourteen trees here stand in Potsdam itself, among them columnar oaks on Bassinplatz and a plane at the kerb on Am Kanal. The other four stand just across the Glienicke bridge on the Berlin bank, a twelve-minute tram ride from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof, inside the UNESCO World Heritage parkland. Only one of the fourteen has a published age.
meta_description: Fourteen protected trees in and around Potsdam: the thousand-year oak at Sacrow, columnar oaks on Bassinplatz, and old limes by the Glienicke bridge.
question_meta: The oldest dated tree near Potsdam is the Jägerhof oak, about 300 years old. The thicker thousand-year oak at Sacrow has never been dated.
question_answer: The oldest dated tree on this page is the oak at the Jägerhof in Volkspark Klein-Glienicke, just across the Glienicke bridge, roughly 300 years old and 566 centimetres round when it was last measured in 2023. Its rival is the thousand-year oak in the Schlosspark Sacrow, which is thicker at 685 centimetres and carries the bigger name, but the thousand years are the register's name for it rather than a measurement, and nobody has published an age for it. The Jägerhof figure comes from a German veteran-tree archive reasoning backwards from the Jägerhof itself, which was built before 1830 with the oak already standing beside it and, in that archive's judgement, already more than a century old. None of the other twelve trees here has a published age, so this page gives them none rather than a guess.
question_context: The trees on this page come from two registers on either side of a bridge. Ten stand in Potsdam itself, on the city's list of natural monuments, which records a number, a girth and a coordinate for each and never an age: three sites in Sacrow, the columnar oaks of Bassinplatz, the plane on Am Kanal, the Weberplatz lime, the Schiffbauergasse oak, the Jungfernsee trio, the Rote Kaserne oak and the sessile oak on the Paetowstrasse. The other four stand on the Berlin bank across the Glienicke bridge, protected by the Land of Berlin, in parkland that is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site of the palaces and parks of Potsdam and Berlin; the tram from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof crosses in twelve minutes. Only the Jägerhof oak has been dated, taped at 566 centimetres in 2023 by a German veteran-tree archive. Several Potsdam trees, among them the Weberplatz lime, the Schiffbauergasse oak and the Am Kanal plane, have no recent dated sighting, so if you pass one, tell us whether it still stands. Three planes in the walled garden behind the Glienicke hunting lodge are left off, because nobody could confirm public access.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree near Potsdam?
faq.a: The oldest dated one is the oak at the Jägerhof in Volkspark Klein-Glienicke, roughly 300 years old. The estimate comes from a German veteran-tree archive, which measured it at 566 centimetres round in 2023 and reasoned back from the Jägerhof, built before 1830 with the oak already standing. The thousand-year oak at Sacrow is thicker, at 685 centimetres, but its age has never been measured; the thousand years are a name.

faq.q: Are these trees actually in Potsdam?
faq.a: Ten of the fourteen are: the thousand-year oak at Sacrow, the roadside oak on the Krampnitzer Strasse, the three Weinmeisterweg oaks, the Bassinplatz oaks, the Am Kanal plane, the Weberplatz lime, the Schiffbauergasse oak, the Jungfernsee trio, the Rote Kaserne oak and the sessile oak on the Paetowstrasse. The other four stand on the Berlin bank of the Havel, in Berlin-Wannsee, immediately across the Glienicke bridge. Tram 93 from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof reaches the bridge in about twelve minutes.

Yes. Twelve stand in open parkland, on public squares, at the roadside, beside a public track, on an open lawn in a housing estate or on the open grounds of the Schiffbauergasse cultural quarter, with no ticket for the trees themselves. The three Jungfernsee oaks are seen from the Bertinistrasse and the shore path; whether any of them stands inside a private fence is not confirmed, so look from the path. The three Weinmeisterweg oaks stand behind the last houses at the forest edge with private gates nearby, so keep to the public way.

faq.q: Can I see them all in one walk?
faq.a: Not all fourteen. The four by the Glienicke bridge make one good walk: the two limes and the first oak are within a few hundred metres of the bridge, and the Jägerhof oak is fifteen to twenty minutes further south along the park path above the Havel. Allow about two hours. Sacrow makes a second: the roadside oak is about 300 metres from the thousand-year oak, and the Weinmeisterweg trio about 500. In the centre, Bassinplatz, the Am Kanal plane and the Schiffbauergasse lie within about a kilometre of each other. The Jungfernsee shore and the Rote Kaserne oak are under a kilometre apart. The Paetowstrasse oak in the Templiner Vorstadt and the Weberplatz lime in Babelsberg are each a separate trip.

trees.name: The Linden of Park Jagdschloss Glienicke

location.address: Park Jagdschloss Glienicke, northwestern section, about 200m southeast of Glienicker Brücke, Königstraße, Berlin-Wannsee (Steglitz-Zehlendorf), on the Potsdam border
location.neighbourhood: Schlosspark Glienicke, Berlin side of the Glienicke Bridge

trees.story: Two hundred metres from this lime tree is the bridge where the Cold War traded people. Glienicker Brücke carried the spy exchanges between the Americans and the Soviets, and the border ran down the middle of the water beneath it. The tree stands on the eastern bank, which is to say in Berlin, though it is a twelve-minute tram ride from Potsdam's main station and a long way from anything a Berliner thinks of as the city. It is a small-leaved lime, a Winter-Linde, protected by the Land of Berlin as a natural monument under the number 6-99/B, standing in the open parkland of Park Jagdschloss Glienicke around the old hunting lodge. What that protection does not come with is information. The register gives a species, a parcel number and a place, and records no age, no girth and no note on the tree's condition, because it is a legal instrument rather than a survey. So this entry is thinner than most here, and it says so. One official source names the tree and nothing else we could find does. What that source does establish is the thing worth walking for: somebody looked at this particular lime, among all the trees in a large park, and decided it was not to be cut down.
trees.how_to_recognise: In the open parkland around the hunting lodge, not in the walled garden behind the building. The second protected lime is 200 metres east, on Königstraße opposite the Wiesenteich pond.
trees.access: Free, open to the public year-round. Stands in Park Jagdschloss Glienicke, the open parkland around the hunting lodge, not the fenced institute garden behind the building itself
trees.transport: Tram 93 from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof to the Glienicker Brücke stop, about 12 minutes, then a short walk into the park
trees.notes: Land Berlin Naturdenkmal register id 6-99/B (Tilia cordata, Winter-Linde), Flur 110037-14-82, matching the official gazette PDF word for word. Flagged: only one source found, the Land Berlin register itself, and no independent second source. The register carries no age or vitality field, which is standard for this dataset.

best_time.label: June to July, when it flowers

trees.name: The King's Linden

location.address: Schlossgarten Glienicke, on Königstraße opposite the Wiesenteich pond, Berlin-Wannsee (Steglitz-Zehlendorf), on the Potsdam border
location.neighbourhood: Schlosspark Glienicke, Berlin side of the Glienicke Bridge

trees.story: People took tea under this lime, and the floor they did it on is still there. A mosaic pavement near the Lions Fountain in the Schlossgarten marks the spot where visitors to Prince Carl of Prussia's estate sat beneath the tree, and the park's own account calls it one of the most impressive solitary trees on the estate. Berlin's register of natural monuments agrees in its own dry way. It gives the tree a number, 6-100/B, and a name, Königslinde, the King's Linden, which is unusual in a document that mostly records species and parcel numbers and then stops. The garden around it was laid out from 1816 by Peter Joseph Lenné for Prince Carl, an English landscape of long sightlines on a Prussian riverbank, and it is now part of the UNESCO World Heritage site covering the palaces and parks of Potsdam and Berlin. It is open, free, and has no gate. Neither the register nor the park's history gives this lime an age or a girth, so it gets neither here. It stands on Königstraße opposite the Wiesenteich pond, on the Berlin side of the Glienicke bridge, twelve minutes from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof on the 93 tram, and it is the tree on this walk that people actually sat under.

best_time.label: late June into July, when the lime blossom opens and the scent carries across the lawn

trees.how_to_recognise: The big solitary lime on the Königstraße side of the Schlossgarten, opposite the Wiesenteich, with the mosaic floor near the Lions Fountain. The other protected lime is 200 metres west, by the hunting lodge.
trees.access: Free, open to the public year-round, no gate, no hours and no admission. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage site of the palaces and parks of Potsdam and Berlin
trees.transport: Tram 93 from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof to the Glienicker Brücke stop, about 12 minutes, then a short walk into the Schlossgarten
trees.notes: Land Berlin Naturdenkmal register id 6-100/B, named Konigslinde in the register itself, Flur 110037-14-85. Second source is English Wikipedia's Park Glienicke article (the solitary-tree description and the tea-party mosaic). Flagged because neither source is a recent dated photograph or observation; the register was pulled from a live Land Berlin geodata service on 2026-08-07. No age or girth in either source.

trees.name: The Schlosspark Glienicke Oak

location.address: Schlosspark Glienicke, about 150m north of Königstraße 35C, Berlin-Wannsee (Steglitz-Zehlendorf), on the Potsdam border
location.neighbourhood: Schlosspark Glienicke, Berlin side of the Glienicke Bridge

trees.story: Berlin protects this oak by law and almost nothing else about it is on record. It appears in the Land of Berlin's register of natural monuments as 6-105/B, a Stiel-Eiche, a Pedunculate Oak, standing about 150 metres north of Königstraße 35C in Schlosspark Glienicke. That entry gives a species, a parcel and a position, and there it ends: no age, no girth, no word on the tree's condition, because the register exists to say what may not be felled rather than to describe what is there. So this is a tree you go and read for yourself. It grows in the landscape garden Peter Joseph Lenné began laying out in 1816 for Prince Carl of Prussia, a park of engineered views designed to look accidental, now inside the UNESCO World Heritage site that covers the palaces and parks of Potsdam and Berlin. Oaks are the long-lived furniture of gardens like this one, and often older than the design around them. The one fact the register does carry says something a tape measure would not: out of the thousands of trees standing in this parkland, somebody walked up to this one and wrote it down. It is a few minutes further into the park than the two protected limes. If you get a tape round it, we would like the number.
trees.access: Free, open to the public year-round, the same parkland as the two limes, part of the UNESCO World Heritage site of the palaces and parks of Potsdam and Berlin
trees.transport: Tram 93 from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof to the Glienicker Brücke stop, about 12 minutes, then a walk of a few minutes further into the park than the lime trees
trees.notes: Land Berlin Naturdenkmal register id 6-105/B (Quercus robur, Stiel-Eiche), Flur 110037-14-130, matching the imported WFS register entry and the official gazette word for word. Flagged: one source only, no independent second source, and no genuine girth or age figure found. A search summary claiming a '130cm circumference' was checked against the source PDF and is the Flur parcel number, not a measurement; it is deliberately not recorded here and must not be reintroduced.

best_time.label: September to October: acorns drop, and a good mast year buries the ground in them

trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the register's protected oak about 150 metres north of Konigstrasse 35C, a short walk past the two protected limes. It stands in Schlosspark Glienicke, on the Potsdam border.

trees.name: The Jägerhof Oak

location.address: Volkspark Klein-Glienicke, at the Jägerhof, south of the Krughorn headland, Berlin-Wannsee (Steglitz-Zehlendorf), on the Potsdam border
location.neighbourhood: Volkspark Klein-Glienicke, Berlin side of the Glienicke Bridge

trees.story: The oak was here first. The Jägerhof in Volkspark Klein-Glienicke went up some time before 1830, and by the reckoning of the German veteran-tree archive that measured this tree, it was already more than a hundred years old when the builders arrived. That puts its beginning before roughly 1730, which makes 300 years a fair estimate and not a precise one. Nobody has cored it, and Berlin's register of natural monuments, which protects it as 6-73/B, has no age field to put a figure in. The girth is firmer: 566 centimetres at chest height, taped in 2023. Nearly six metres of trunk, and by a wide margin the heaviest tree on this walk. It stands high above the Havel path near the Krughorn headland, south along the park from the Glienicke bridge and about fifteen to twenty minutes on foot from the other three trees here. Berlin bought the estate in the 1930s and opened it to the public, so the ground under this oak has been walkable for the better part of a century. Before that it was hunting country, which is what a Jägerhof is for. The lodge was built for the sport. The oak was simply standing in the way of it, and outlived the whole arrangement.

best_time.label: January and February, when the leaves are down and the whole frame of the old crown shows

verified_sources: https://www.ostdeutsches-baumarchiv.de/photosearch/eiche-jaegerhof-glienicke-berlin (circumference 566 cm at 1.3 m, measured 2023; Naturdenkmal per NDVO Berlin)
trees.access: Free, open to the public. Volkspark Klein-Glienicke was opened to the public in the 1930s when Berlin acquired the estate; the Jägerhof and the ground around it are publicly accessible, high above the Havel-side path near the Krughorn
trees.transport: Tram 93 from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof to the Glienicker Brücke stop, about 12 minutes, then roughly a 15-20 minute walk south along the park path to the Jägerhof
trees.notes: Land Berlin Naturdenkmal register id 6-73/B (Quercus robur, Stiel-Eiche). Second, independent source: Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv, a German veteran-tree archive unaffiliated with the Berlin government, giving 566cm girth measured 2023 at 1.3m and a photo dated 2011. The age follows that archive's own reasoning (Jagerhof built before 1830, oak likely already over 100 years old then), so 250-350 is a source-grounded range rather than an invented figure. The strongest-evidenced of the four.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the heaviest tree on this walk, 5.66 metres round. It stands high above the Havel path near the Krughorn headland in Volkspark Klein-Glienicke.

trees.name: The Thousand-Year Oak of Sacrow
trees.story:
Potsdam's register calls this the thousand-year oak, and nobody has ever counted the thousand years. The name is the city's own designation for natural monument number 15, and it is a title rather than a date: the same register gives the tree a girth and a coordinate and leaves the age field out entirely.

The girth is the part that holds. At 685 centimetres round, close to seven metres of trunk, it is the thickest oak on Potsdam's whole list of natural monuments. Two more protected oaks stand a short walk away along the Krampnitzer Strasse, at 600 and 575 centimetres, and this one still outweighs them both. A pedunculate oak of that size is old by any reckoning. How old is a question a tape measure alone cannot settle, and the register does not try.

It stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, the landscape park on the Havel shore laid out to a design by Lenné, open to walk in daylight and free. Someone photographed the spot in June 2025, which is the most recent sign of life on record, though the register does not say when its girth was taken.

So the honest version is this: Potsdam's thickest protected oak, wearing a name it may or may not have earned. If you know when it was last measured, or have a better idea of its age, tell us.
verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkmale_in_Potsdam (reproduces the city's Naturdenkmal list: no. 15, girth 685 cm, coordinates, Flurstueck 118/14)
trees.access: Free. Stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, a public landscape park by the Havel (Lenne design); open in daylight.
trees.transport: By bus from central Potsdam to Sacrow, then on foot through the Schlosspark Sacrow to the oak.
trees.notes: Register only (official Potsdam Naturdenkmal list via de.wikipedia reproduction), one source for species and girth. Girth 685 cm is the thickest of the Potsdam oak monuments, from the register's Umfang column, no measurement date given. The name '1000-jaehrige Eiche' is the register's own designation, NOT a measured age: do not state 1000 years as fact, say 'known as the thousand-year oak'. No age field in the register. Commons has its own category 'Tausendjaehrige Eiche (Sacrow)' and photographs (file 1000-jaehrige Eiche in Sacrow, 1.jpg), so a photograph is in reach. Alive: iNaturalist observation 2025-06-29 at the coordinate (RECENT per lifecheck; proves something photographed there, not the trunk). Note the register's neighbouring Sacrow oaks nos. 13 and 14 (600 and 575 cm, Krampnitzer Strasse) have swapped Commons file labels (ND 13/ND 14), so identity of those two is ambiguous; left as leads.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, 6.85 metres round, thicker than the two protected oaks a short walk away on the Krampnitzer Strasse. It stands in the Schlosspark Sacrow, by the Havel.

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Nr. 15 (Landeshauptstadt Potsdam), no. Naturdenkmal Nr. 15

trees.name: The Columnar Oaks of Bassinplatz
trees.story:
Most oaks spread. These two go straight up. The pair on Bassinplatz are fastigiate oaks, a columnar form of the ordinary pedunculate oak that holds its branches close to the trunk and grows like a flame rather than a dome. Potsdam protects both as natural monuments, numbers 31 and 32, standing about forty metres apart on the same square.

The surprise is in the register's tape measure. It gives the larger one 600 centimetres round, six metres of trunk, which is a girth you expect from a broad veteran in open parkland and not from a cultivar bred to stay narrow. The second comes in at a more ordinary 395. We have not been able to check the bigger figure, and a number that size on a columnar tree could be a measurement taken around more than one stem, so read it as the register's word until somebody confirms it.

What is not in doubt is that both are standing: each was photographed in June 2026. The register gives neither of them an age, and nothing else we have found does either.

They make an odd sight in a city square, two green columns where you would expect a spreading crown, and they are among the easiest protected trees in Potsdam to reach, on open public ground in the centre. If you know how old they are, or have run a tape around the big one yourself, tell us.
trees.access: Free. A public city square in central Potsdam, open at all times.
trees.transport: In central Potsdam, a short walk from the Brandenburger Tor.
trees.notes: FOLDED twin: register nos. 31 (52.401872, 13.062176, girth 600 cm) and 32 (52.40203, 13.06268, girth 395 cm) both on Flurstueck 692, about 40 m apart; shown as one stop, pin on no. 31. Register only, one source. Both are fastigiate (columnar) oaks, a cultivar, which is the point of them: an upright form of the English oak on a square. 600 cm girth is large for a fastigiate cultivar, which is a plain register figure, unverified by us (a girth like this on a columnar form is unusual; flagged in case it is a multi-stem measurement). No age in register; do not derive one. Alive: two iNaturalist observations dated 2026-06-18 at the two coordinates (RECENT). Photographs in reach on Commons (files named Naturdenkmal Nr. 31 / Nr. 32 Saeulen-Eiche auf dem Bassinplatz).
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise them by their shape: two narrow, upright oaks where you would expect broad crowns. They stand on Bassinplatz about 40 metres apart; the pin marks the thicker one, 6 metres round.

official_register.name: Naturdenkmal Nr. 31 und Nr. 32 (Landeshauptstadt Potsdam), no. Naturdenkmal Nr. 31, Nr. 32

trees.name: The Lime of Weberplatz

location.address: Weberplatz, beside the Friedrichskirche (Bohemian church), in front of the sacristy, 14482 Potsdam

trees.story:
Potsdam's register places this lime with unusual precision: by the church, in front of the sacristy. Most entries give a street. This one tells you which door to stand at.

It is a small-leaved lime, natural monument number 53, which the register measures at 380 centimetres round, close to four metres of trunk on a city square in Babelsberg. The register gives it no age, and we have found nobody who has dated it, so this page does not guess.

Weberplatz holds a second protected tree about seventy metres away, a white mulberry of nearly the same girth at the corner of the Lutherstrasse, and it is worth a look on the way past.

Here is the gap we will not paper over. The most recent photograph we can find of this spot dates from 2011, and it shows the square rather than this trunk. The lime is still on the register, but we cannot show you dated proof that it stands today, and a register is a list of what was protected rather than a report on what survived.

So this is a tree to check as much as to collect. If you pass the church on Weberplatz, look in front of the sacristy, and tell us whether the lime is still there. In early summer, if it is, you will smell it before you see it.

best_time.label: late June into July, when the lime flowers and the scent carries across the square

Alive check weak: lifecheck returned OLD (2011) within the radius, and that Commons photo is of the square, not necessarily this trunk; no recent dated confirmation found, so the page should ask readers to confirm it still stands. The register's own place text 'an der Kirche vor der Sakristei' places it by the church, which is a clear recognition line. trees.name: The Oak of the Schiffbauergasse

location.address: Schiffbauergasse cultural site, Berliner Strasse 28, 14467 Potsdam

trees.story:
This oak has a theatre for a neighbour. It stands on the grounds of the Schiffbauergasse, Potsdam's cultural quarter on the shore of the Tiefer See, where the evening crowd comes for a play, a meal or the lakeside walk and can easily walk straight past a protected tree.

The register lists it as natural monument number 29, a pedunculate oak measured at 480 centimetres round. Nearly five metres of trunk puts it among the larger oaks the city protects, though well behind the thousand-year oak at Sacrow, which tapes 685. Nobody has recorded its age, and we have found no source that tries, so this page leaves the number empty rather than inventing one.

There is a second gap, and it matters more. The most recent dated picture we can find from this spot is from 2009, and it looks out over the lake rather than at the trunk. The oak is still on the register, but we cannot show you recent proof that it stands, and a register records what was protected, not what survived.

The grounds themselves are open to the public, so checking is easy: come for the lake or the theatre and look for the big oak on the way. If it is there, or if it is not, tell us. Either answer makes this page better.
trees.access: Free. Stands on the grounds of the Schiffbauergasse cultural quarter on the Tiefer See, which is open to the public (theatre, restaurants, lakeside walk); not checked against opening times of individual venues.
trees.transport: On the Tiefer See waterfront in the Berliner Vorstadt, at the Schiffbauergasse cultural quarter.
trees.notes: Register only, one source. Alive check weak: lifecheck returned OLD (2009) and the matched Commons file is a view of the Tiefer See, not clearly this trunk, so recent proof of life is missing and the page should ask readers. Commons has a dedicated photograph (Naturdenkmal Nr 29 Stiel-Eiche auf dem Gelaende der Schiffbauergasse.jpg), so a photograph is in reach. Pin is the register coordinate; I did not check it against imagery, so call it confirmed only because it is the register's tree-level point. If the writer or a later pass finds the point lands off the crown, downgrade to approximate. No age in register.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the large oak on the Schiffbauergasse grounds by the Tiefer See, 4.8 metres round; the pin is the register's own point for this tree.

trees.name: The Oaks of the Jungfernsee

location.address: Bertinistrasse, on the shore of the Jungfernsee, 14467 Potsdam

trees.story:
Three oaks share one entry in Potsdam's register, and the register will not tell you which is which. Natural monument number 19 is a trio of pedunculate oaks strung along about 150 metres of the Jungfernsee shore by the Bertinistrasse, with girths of 460, 515 and 590 centimetres and three separate coordinates. What it does not record is which girth belongs to which point.

That turns the biggest of them, close to six metres round, into a small puzzle for whoever comes to look: it is one of these three, and a tape measure is the only way to settle which. Our pin sits on the northernmost of the register's three points, which is why this page marks it as approximate. Walk the shore and all three stand along the same stretch.

They were photographed together in April 2025, so all three were standing then. Nobody has recorded an age for any of them, and we have not found a source that guesses.

One more honest note. The register puts them on three different land parcels, and we have not confirmed whether any of them stands behind a private fence. Look from the street and the shore path, and leave the gardens alone. If you can tell us which of the three is the 590, or roughly how old they are, please do.
verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkmale_in_Potsdam (no. 19, three oaks, girths 460, 515 and 590 cm, three coordinates)
trees.access: Free to see from the Bertinistrasse and the shore path by the lake. The register places the three oaks on three separate land parcels, and whether any of them stands inside a fenced private plot has not been confirmed, so look from the street and the path.
trees.transport: On the Jungfernsee shore north of the centre, along the Bertinistrasse.
trees.notes: Register only, one source. Three oaks, register points 52.429927,13.064992 / 52.429316,13.064753 / 52.428601,13.064674, spread over about 150 m along the shore: a trio read as one stop, not a single trunk. Girths 460, 515 and 590 cm, but the register does not say which point carries which girth, so the thickest cannot be pinned individually: pin is the northernmost point and precision is approximate for that reason. trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as three large oaks spread over about 150 metres of the Jungfernsee shore by the Bertinistrasse. The pin is the northernmost; the thickest, 5.9 metres round, is one of the three.

trees.name: The Sessile Oak of Paetowstrasse

location.address: Paetowstrasse, southern unpaved section by the Kolonie Sternschanze allotments, 14473 Potsdam

trees.story:
Four and a half metres of sessile oak stand beside a dirt track, at the edge of an allotment colony in the Templiner Vorstadt. Potsdam lists it as natural monument number 39 and gives two reasons for protecting it: its scientific value, and its character and beauty.

The girth is the number everyone agrees on. The city's own page, the German Wikipedia list of Potsdam's natural monuments and the OpenStreetMap entry all give 450 centimetres. The city's page adds that the species can reach six metres round, which puts this one three quarters of the way there.

It is also easy to find. The unpaved southern stretch of the Paetowstrasse runs past the Kolonie Sternschanze allotments, and the oak stands about five metres off the track. A photograph from January 2021 and a map entry from the same year put it on exactly the same spot, which is why the pin here sits on the tree. The coordinate in the public list of Potsdam's monuments is about 26 metres out.

The thin part is the recent past. That 2021 photograph is the latest sighting we have, and nobody has published an age for the tree. If you walk past, tell us it still stands, and if you know how old it is, tell us that too.

The Hauptbahnhof is about 20 minutes away on foot. Some 80 to 100 metres south-west, the register lists a group of Turkey oaks as monument number 40.
trees.access: Free, open at all times: the oak stands about 5 m from a public unpaved track (OSM highway=track, no access restriction), the unpaved southern section of Paetowstrasse beside the allotment colony. No fee, no opening hours.
trees.transport: About 1.5 km (20 minutes on foot) from Potsdam Hauptbahnhof; city buses on Templiner Strasse about 600 m away (stop not checked)

Page text on species (up to 600 cm girth, 800 to 1000 years) is generic, not about this tree. Girth 450 cm agrees with OSM circumference=4.50 and de.wikipedia list Umfang 450. Flagged: alive evidence is a January 2021 photo and the 2021 OSM node, lifecheck.py returned NONE, no newer observation found; register-only vitality. Neighbours: Naturdenkmal Nr. 40 (Zerr-Eichen, Quercus cerris, girths 160 to 295 cm, 5 or more trees, OSM nodes near 52.3809,13.0513, about 80 to 100 m south-west) is a separate ensemble not verified here and would make a pair to walk. No age source. Not checked: Wayback copy of city page; fetched live 2026-10-14.

trees.name: The Three Oaks of the Weinmeisterweg

location.address: End of Weinmeisterweg, behind the last houses at the forest edge, 14469 Potsdam

trees.story:
A German tree archive says one of the trunks here is really two oaks grown into one. Potsdam protects three pedunculate oaks behind the last houses of the Weinmeisterweg in Sacrow as natural monument number 12, and gives them girths of 470, 560 and 650 centimetres. The Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv, a private record of old trees, counted them differently on its 2021 visit: one oak at 589 centimetres, and a twin, fused at the base and grown together above chest height, which it could only tape as a single trunk of 673.

The two sets of numbers do not quite meet. The twin comes out larger than the register's biggest oak, which fits a tree that kept growing after the city measured it, or a tape held at another height. The register does not say when it measured, so both figures stand here and neither is corrected into the other.

The city protects them for science, rarity, distinctiveness and beauty. It gives no age, and nobody we have found has dated them.

Getting there means passing the last houses at the forest edge. The map shows a bollard on the way in that lets walkers through, with private gates and a private service road close by. Keep to the public way and out of the gardens.

The latest sighting we know of is that 2021 visit. If you go, tell us they still stand. The thousand-year oak in the Schlosspark is about 500 metres away.

trees.access: Free to see. The oaks stand west of the Weinmeisterweg, behind the last houses at the forest edge; OSM shows a foot-passable bollard (foot=yes, motor_vehicle=no) on the way in, and also private gates and a private service road nearby, so approach on the public way and stay off fenced gardens.
trees.transport: Sacrow, north of Potsdam; reached by city bus to Sacrow then a short walk along the Weinmeisterweg (stop not checked). About 500 m (straight line) from the Thousand-Year Oak in the Schlosspark Sacrow.
trees.notes: City page (fetched 2026-10-20): Naturdenkmal Nr. 12, three Stiel-Eichen (Quercus robur), 'westlich des Weinmeisterweges, hinter den Grundstuecken am Waldrand', Flur 2 Flurstueck 63, girths 470, 560 and 650 cm, protected for science, rarity, distinctiveness and beauty. Three OSM tree nodes (mapped 2021, edited 2025-01) sit within about 25 m: 52.4315332,13.0954604 (circumference 6.50), 52.4314280,13.0955010 (5.60), 52.4313363,13.0955364 (4.70). Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv (private archive, not an authority; visits 2010 and 2021) measured in 2021: one oak 589 cm (GPS 52.431541,13.095478) and a 'Zwillingseiche' (two oaks grown together at the base, overgrowth above 1.3 m, so measured as one) 673 cm, listed with the two neighbours; both photographed 2021. The 673 cm twin exceeds the register's 650 cm, consistent with growth since the register measurement (date not given) or a different measuring height; both figures recorded, do not merge. Standort per Baumarchiv: 'Am Weinmeisterweg, linkerhand hinter den letzten Haeusern'. trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise them as three big oaks within about 25 metres of each other, behind the last houses at the forest edge west of the Weinmeisterweg. The pin is on the thickest, 6.5 metres round.

trees.name: The Roadside Oak of Sacrow

location.address: Krampnitzer Strasse, opposite the Faehrstrasse junction, 14469 Potsdam

trees.story:
One tree archive has come back to this roadside oak seven times since 2000, most recently in 2021. Natural monument number 14 is a pedunculate oak on the Krampnitzer Strasse in Sacrow, roughly opposite the turning into the Fährstrasse, and nothing about it is behind a gate: you see it from the street.

Potsdam's register gives it 575 centimetres round. The Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv, a private record of old trees in eastern Germany, taped 596 in 2021. The gap fits a tree that grew after the city measured it, or a tape held at another height, so both numbers are kept.

The archive also lists the paperwork behind it: an ordinance for the old Osthavelland district in 1949, and the Potsdam ordinance of 2005 that protects it today. Neither the register nor the archive gives it an age, and we have not found anyone who has.

One warning about the pin. The register's coordinate sits by the Fährstrasse junction, which matches both written descriptions, but an online map puts the tree about 55 metres further east, and we have not settled which is right. So our pin is approximate. Go by the junction instead: the archive puts the oak about 20 metres north of it, just before the Fährstrasse comes in.

The thousand-year oak in the Schlosspark is about 300 metres to the west. If you know this tree's age, tell us.
trees.access: Free, open at all times: stands by the public Krampnitzer Strasse (OSM highway=residential), seen from the road.
trees.transport: Sacrow, north of Potsdam; city bus to Sacrow (stop not checked). About 300 m (straight line) east of the Thousand-Year Oak in the Schlosspark Sacrow.
trees.notes: City page (fetched 2026-10-20): Naturdenkmal Nr. 14, Stiel-Eiche (Quercus robur) in Sacrow, 'Krampnitzer Strasse, etwa gegenueber der Einfahrt Faehrstrasse', Flur 1 Flurstueck 18, girth 575 cm, protected for science, distinctiveness, rarity and beauty. Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv (private archive, not an authority; visits 2000, 2006, 2009, 2010, 2015, 2019, 2021): 'an der Krampnitzer Strasse, ca. 20 m noerdlich kurz vor der Einmuendung der Faehrstrasse', girth 596 cm in 2021 with a 2021 photograph; cites the 1949 Osthavelland ordinance, Froehlich 1994 and the 2005 Potsdam ordinance. 596 cm (2021) against the register's 575 cm is consistent with growth or a different measuring height; both recorded. Pin: register list coordinate 52.428604,13.096611 equals the Commons geotag (2018, same figure, so not independent) and lies about 8 m from the OSM Faehrstrasse junction node (52.42854,13.09651), agreeing with both texts. OSM tree node 8678713311 (circumference 5.75, edited 2025-08-18) sits about 55 m further east at 52.4287381,13.0974103: unexplained conflict, so the pin is kept approximate and the crown is to be found at the junction, not by coordinate. Alive: Baumarchiv visit and photo in 2021 and the OSM node edit in 2025; lifecheck.py not run on this point. Registers carry no vitality. No age source. Sibling Naturdenkmal Nr. 13 (Krampnitzer Strasse 17, girth 600 cm, shore of the Sacrower See, 52.428776,13.089546) is NOT delivered: Commons photo says the trunk is hidden behind a fence and bushes from the street, so access is not established; recorded as a lead. trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the big oak at the roadside of the Krampnitzer Strasse, about 20 metres north of where the Fährstrasse joins it. The pin is approximate, so trust the junction over the dot.

trees.name: The Plane of Am Kanal

location.address: Am Kanal, across from no. 71, at the roadside, 14467 Potsdam

trees.story:
This natural monument is a street tree. Potsdam protected it on 21 November 2005 as number 33, and the city's own page places it with the precision of a delivery note: in the street Am Kanal, opposite number 71, at the roadside.

It is a London plane, the hybrid that lines city streets across Europe, and the city's page marks it as a foreign species. That is part of what makes it odd company. Every other Potsdam tree on this page is an oak or a lime, standing in a park, on a square or at a forest edge. This one stands at a kerb in the middle of town, and made the list anyway.

The city's page gives its girth as 423 centimetres; the German Wikipedia list of Potsdam's monuments says 426. Three centimetres is a small enough gap to be a tape held a little higher or lower, and both figures are on record. Either way, more than four metres of trunk at the edge of a road.

Nobody has published an age for it, so this page gives none. The most recent photographs we know of were uploaded in December 2020, which is thin proof for today. If you walk past, tell us it still stands.

The columnar oaks on Bassinplatz are about 550 metres away, which makes the two an easy pair for a walk through the centre.
trees.access: Free, open at all times: stands on the street edge of the public road Am Kanal, seen from the pavement.
trees.transport: Central Potsdam; about 550 m (straight line) from Bassinplatz, the tram and bus hub, which is also where the Bassinplatz columnar oaks stand.
trees.notes: City page (fetched 2026-10-20): Naturdenkmal Nr. 33, Ahornblaettrige Platane (Platanus x acerifolia), 'in der Strasse Am Kanal 71, gegenueber am Strassenrand' (foreign species), Flur 25 Flurstueck 649, girth 423 cm on the page (426 cm in the de.wikipedia list; both recorded). Designation 2005-11-21 (Wikidata, citing Amtsblatt 14/2005). Pin: OSM natural=tree node 8689994872 (denotation natural_monument, circumference 4.23, edited 2025-01-24, with Commons image link) at 52.3989831,13.0690061 equals the register coordinate to 6 decimals, so the two are not independent; they agree with the city's text 'opposite no. 71 at the roadside', a single street tree, hence confirmed, but not checked against imagery: downgrade to approximate if a later pass finds it off the crown. Am Kanal A to D); photograph date not read; the OSM node was edited 2025-01 but that is not a sighting. lifecheck.py returned NONE, so flagged for thin recent confirmation. Register-only for species and girth; no age source, do not derive one. A photograph is in reach on Commons (CC licence not read for this pass). Part of a central Potsdam walk with pot_006 (Bassinplatz oaks).

trees.name: The Oak of the Rote Kaserne

location.address: Former Rote Kaserne, opposite the school, Fritz-von-der-Lancken-Strasse, 14469 Potsdam

trees.story:
Potsdam lists this oak as natural monument number 10. The tree archive that has visited it nine times since 2009 says it is not a natural monument at all.

The disagreement may be paperwork rather than anything about the tree. The city's own list carries it, and Wikidata records its designation in November 2005; the archive's entry began as a find in 2009 and may simply never have caught up. We go by the city's list, and we say that is where the protection comes from.

It stands in the northern part of the former Rote Kaserne, the Red Barracks, a site since rebuilt as new housing and a school. The archive describes a solitary oak on open lawn with a playground, across from the school, and the paths of the housing estate are the way in.

The tape gives two answers. The city's page says 505 centimetres round; the archive measured 550 at chest height in 2023. That fits a tree that grew after the city's measurement, or a tape held at another height, and both figures are kept. The archive also records that the crown has been cut back several times in recent years.

Nobody has published a reliable age for it, so this page gives none. If you know how old it is, tell us. The last visit we know of was in 2023.
trees.access: Free. Per Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv ('Zugang: Frei zugaenglich', visited 2009 to 2023) the oak stands on open lawn with a playground between new housing and a school on the former barracks site; the site was redeveloped, so the housing estate's paths are the way in. Not checked against OSM access tags or a city source.
trees.transport: Potsdam Nord, former Rote Kaserne off Fritz-von-der-Lancken-Strasse near the Nedlitzer Strasse (stops not checked).
trees.notes: Register: city page (fetched 2026-10-20, Flur 1 Flurstueck 293, girth 505 cm, 'im noerdlichen Teil der ehemaligen Roten Kaserne', Fritz-von-der-Lancken-Strasse); designation 2005-11-21 per Wikidata; de.wikipedia list coordinate 52.427162,13.056581. Ostdeutsches Baumarchiv (private archive, not an authority): solitary Stiel-Eiche 'gegenueber der Schule', visited 2009, 2010, 2014, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and twice in 2023, girth 550 cm at 1.3 m in 2023, photo 2021, GPS 52.427162,13.056471. Two independent coordinates 10 m apart on a solitary crown: pin set between them, confirmed. DISCREPANCIES to keep: (1) register page 505 cm against archive 550 cm in 2023, consistent with growth or different measuring height, both recorded; (2) the archive says 'Naturdenkmal: Nein' while the city still lists it as Nr. 10; the archive entry is a 2009 find and may simply not know the designation, but it should not be stated on the page that it is protected without noting the city's own list is the source. (3) archive notes the crown has been repeatedly cut back in recent years. History per the archive (not a verified source, do not use as fact): barracks built 1892 to 1895 around the tree, Soviet army until 1993, now housing, a school and playground. The archive's remark that the oak must have been about 100 years old in 1892 is the archive's inference, a bridge, NOT an age source: leave age empty. Alive: archive visits through 2023 with a 2021 photograph; lifecheck.py returned NONE. A Commons category 'Roten Kaserne (Potsdam)' holds the Naturdenkmal photograph, not viewed.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the lone big oak on the open lawn with the playground, across from the school in the northern part of the former Rote Kaserne. Its trunk is about 5.5 metres round.
